slot.brief: Provide the figure of d-orbital splitting (octahedral) with electron occupancy for a given metal ion; ask to match it with the correct complex from options and state high/low spin and magnetic character.

stem: The octahedral splitting shown in the figure corresponds to which complex and its spin and magnetic character?

verdicts.working: The diagram shows a low-spin d⁶ configuration: t₂g⁶e_g⁰, with all electrons paired. Fe²⁺ in [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ is d⁶; CN⁻ is a strong-field ligand, so the complex is low-spin and diamagnetic.

working:
Six $d$ electrons occupy the lower $t_{2g}$ orbitals: $t_{2g}^{6}e_g^{0}$.\nFor $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, $d^6$; $\text{CN}^-$ gives low-spin $t_{2g}^{6}e_g^{0}$, with zero unpaired electrons.

Independent check: The diagram shows a low-spin d⁶ configuration: t₂g⁶e_g⁰, with all electrons paired. Fe²⁺ in [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ is d⁶; CN⁻ is a strong-field ligand, so the complex is low-spin and diamagnetic.
solution:
In $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$, iron is in the $+2$ oxidation state, giving a $d^6$ configuration. Since $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong-field ligand, the electrons pair in the lower $t_{2g}$ orbitals:
$$t_{2g}^{6}e_g^{0}$$
All electrons are paired, so the complex is low-spin and diamagnetic.

figure.description: Draw an octahedral crystal-field splitting diagram. Include a vertical energy axis with an upward arrow labelled E. Show a lower horizontal level labelled t2g with three separate orbital boxes; put one upward and one downward arrow in each box. Show an upper horizontal level labelled eg with two separate empty orbital boxes. Do not include a complex formula or labels for spin or magnetic character.

draft.working: Six $d$ electrons occupy the lower $t_{2g}$ orbitals: $t_{2g}^{6}e_g^{0}$.\nFor $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, $d^6$; $\text{CN}^-$ gives low-spin $t_{2g}^{6}e_g^{0}$, with zero unpaired electrons.
draft.distractor_notes:
B: $\text{F}^-$ gives high-spin $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, not the shown occupancy.
C: $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ is $d^3$, not $d^6$.
D: $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ is $d^8$ and occupies the upper $e_g$ level.
